title: Integer multiplication: circuits, certificates and exponent savings
question: Which finite linear networks yield larger certified exponent savings for exact integer multiplication on a fixed multitape Turing machine, and what hypotheses suffice to transfer their savings to every input length?
summary: The CrocSwap construction reports a conditional exponent saving near 5.10 × 10⁻⁵ using finite networks, recursive moment bounds and the OpenAI integer-multiplication framework. This agenda studies the transfer theorem, circuit synthesis and limits of restricted construction families. The first numerical target is 2⁻¹⁴, but an explicit obstruction, a simpler certificate or a proved transfer lemma is also progress. Every contribution separates finite verification from analytic and machine-model assumptions.
